tour.overview:
Venice was built on more than a hundred small islands in a lagoon, on millions of wooden piles driven into the mud. For a thousand years it was an independent republic ruled by an elected Doge, a sea power whose ships carried silk, spices and ideas between Europe and the East. Its wealth paid for golden churches, marble palaces and painters such as Titian, Tintoretto and Veronese. Venice and its lagoon have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.

Cars cannot enter Venice, so this private day is on foot and on the water, with a licensed Venetian guide. You see St Mark's Basilica and the Doge's Palace early, before the crowds fill the square, cross the Bridge of Sighs from the inside, then leave the main routes for the quiet canals of Castello and San Polo. After a lunch of cicchetti, you take a private gondola ride and finish with a water taxi along the Grand Canal, the most beautiful street in the world.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 7 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Venice, the railway station or the cruise terminal
• Type: private walking tour with licensed guide, gondola and water taxi
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 5 km on foot with many small bridges and steps

WHAT YOU SEE
• St Mark's Square and the Campanile (outside).
• St Mark's Basilica.
• The Doge's Palace, its prisons and the Bridge of Sighs.
• The quiet canals of Castello and San Polo.
• The Rialto Bridge and market.
• The Grand Canal by gondola and water taxi.

WHY THIS WORKS
We enter the Doge's Palace at opening time and St Mark's with a reserved slot, then spend the busy middle of the day in neighbourhoods most visitors never find.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors, couples, families and cruise passengers who want to see the best of Venice in one day.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you have seen the centre before, ask us for a private boat day to the islands of Murano, Burano and Torcello.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
On certain days in spring and summer, Venice charges an access fee to day visitors who are not staying overnight; we tell you if your date is affected. Large backpacks are not allowed in St Mark's Basilica. In autumn and winter, high water (acqua alta) can flood St Mark's Square for a few hours.

days.name: St Mark's Basilica, the Doge's Palace and Bridge of Sighs, hidden canals, Rialto, cicchetti lunch, gondola and Grand Canal
days.description:
What to expect: the heart of the Venetian Republic and its quiet canals, with a licensed guide, reserved tickets, a gondola ride, a water taxi and lunch.

Your guide meets you at your hotel, the station or the cruise terminal at about 8:30 and walks you into St Mark's Square, which Napoleon is said to have called the finest drawing room in Europe. You start at the Doge's Palace at opening time. Behind its pink and white Gothic façade, you climb the Golden Staircase to the rooms where the Republic was governed: the Senate, the Council of Ten, which judged in secret, and the Hall of the Great Council, one of the largest rooms in Europe, where Tintoretto's Paradise covers the whole end wall. You then cross the Bridge of Sighs into the old prisons, where Casanova was locked up before his famous escape in 1756, and look out through the stone grilles at the lagoon, as prisoners did for the last time.

With your reserved slot, you enter St Mark's Basilica, consecrated in 1094 to hold the relics of the evangelist Mark, smuggled out of Alexandria by Venetian merchants. More than 8,000 square metres of golden mosaics cover the domes and vaults, glowing above a floor of inlaid marble that rises and falls with the settling of the ground. Your guide shows you the Pala d'Oro, the golden altarpiece set with enamels and jewels, which can be added.

Leaving the crowds behind, you walk through the quiet lanes and squares of Castello and cross into San Polo to the Rialto Bridge, built in stone in 1591, and its market, where Venetians have bought fish and vegetables for a thousand years. Lunch is in a bacaro, a traditional wine bar, with cicchetti – salt cod on polenta, sardines in saor and little sandwiches – and a glass of local wine or a spritz. In the afternoon you board a private gondola for about 30 minutes through the narrow canals, under small bridges and past palace water gates. Finally, a private water taxi carries you along the Grand Canal, past the palaces, the Rialto and the dome of the Salute, to your hotel, the station or the port, at about 15:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Meeting with your guide.
09:00 – Doge's Palace, the prisons and the Bridge of Sighs (about 1 hour 30 minutes).
10:45 – St Mark's Basilica (about 45 minutes).
11:30 – Walk through Castello and San Polo.
12:30 – Rialto Bridge and market.
13:00 – Cicchetti lunch.
14:15 – Private gondola ride (about 30 minutes).
15:00 – Water taxi along the Grand Canal.
15:30 – Arrival at your hotel, the station or the port.

GOOD TO KNOW
• St Mark's Basilica can close at short notice for religious services; we then reorder the day.
• The gondola fits up to five people; larger groups use two gondolas.
• The basilica's museum and terrace, with the bronze horses, can be added.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, Doge's Palace ticket, reserved basilica entry, private gondola, private water taxi, lunch, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: Pala d'Oro and St Mark's museum, Venice day-visitor access fee where it applies, extra drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Why is there no car?
faq.answer: Venice has no roads, only canals and footpaths. You walk with your guide and use a private gondola and water taxi; the price tiers cover the boats and guiding for your group size.

faq.question: Do we skip the lines?
faq.answer: Yes. We reserve entry to St Mark's Basilica and book the Doge's Palace at opening time, so you avoid the long queues. There is a short security check for everyone.

faq.question: Do we have to pay the Venice access fee?
faq.answer: On certain days in spring and summer, day visitors who are not staying overnight in Venice pay an access fee online. Hotel guests are exempt. We tell you if your date is affected and how to register.

faq.question: Is the gondola private?
faq.answer: Yes. You have your own gondola for about 30 minutes. One gondola holds up to five people; larger groups use two.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a cicchetti lunch in a traditional bacaro with a drink. Vegetarian and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: About 5 km, flat but with many small bridges with steps. The water taxi brings you back at the end.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the gondola, the prison and the boats. We keep the museum visits short.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Venice is difficult with a wheelchair because of the bridges, but some routes avoid steps and the water taxi can reach many places. Tell us your needs and we will plan the day with you.

faq.question: What happens if there is high water?
faq.answer: In autumn and winter, acqua alta can flood the lowest areas for a few hours. Raised walkways are set up, and we change the route if needed.

faq.question: Can you meet us at the cruise terminal?
faq.answer: Yes. We meet you at the terminal and plan the day so you are back well before the ship's all-aboard time.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes. For St Mark's Basilica, shoulders and knees must be covered, and large backpacks must be left in a cloakroom nearby.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour, because reserved tickets and the gondola are non-refundable after that. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
